trust_decision.summary: Whether a command submitted to the shell_exec tool runs at all, and as which executable, is decided by SecurityValidator.validateCommand (security.go:25-57) from the SecurityConfig that loadConfig (config.go:44-74) built - and that decision is vacuous both because the built-in default is Enabled:false (config.go:48-50) and because the policy file the shipped Docker image points at lists /bin/bash, /usr/bin/python3 and /usr/bin/git (security.yaml:27-29 via Dockerfile:64-68), so an allowlisted interpreter receives whatever it is handed.

landing_point.why: The summary names the default /bin/bash executable; this shipped YAML is what the image sets as the policy (Dockerfile:64-68), so an engineer reads this allowlist first and sees /bin/bash beside /usr/bin/python3 and /usr/bin/git.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A YAML file is the operator's own policy, so the loader overwriting the built-in defaults with the file's zero values (including Enabled) reads as 'their choice', and the advisory's own claim is only about what ships by default.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An explicitly allowlisted git with blocked_patterns must keep letting `git status` through (security_test.go:117-127), and loadConfig must keep accepting a user file's absolute-path entries such as /usr/bin/git (config_test.go:302-316); a hard ban on interpreter/alias-capable names in the loader breaks the project's own tests, so the legitimate move is warn-and-remove-from-shipped-default, not reject.

O6_input_shapes: bare executable name in the allowlist (e.g. "bash", "git") vs absolute path ("/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/python3") - the fix normalises with filepath.Base
interpreter family: bash/sh/zsh/fish/dash/ksh/csh/tcsh, python/python2/python3, perl, ruby, node, php, plus alias-capable git
argument-level alias shape: `git -c alias.x=!cmd` ('!' added to metacharacters, "=!" added to dangerous constructs)
enablement shape: no config file (built-in defaults) vs MCP_SHELL_SEC_CONFIG_FILE provided vs explicit MCP_SHELL_ALLOW_UNSAFE=true opt-out

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A user config file that allowlists an interpreter (`allowed_executables: [/bin/bash]`): validateExecutableCommand matches it and the executor runs `bash -c <anything>`; the published fix only logs a warning and never refuses (fix.diff:329-340).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the operator's explicit policy, the upstream fix itself only warns, and refusing it breaks the project's own config_test.go:302-316 - a credible 'not our call' dismissal.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one file away from the landing point (security.yaml -> security.go); the fix's only response is the startup warning at fix.diff:329-340

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A YAML config file that omits `enabled: true` (e.g. one that only sets blocked_patterns): loadSecurityFromFile overwrites the whole Security struct with the file's zero values, so Enabled becomes false, validateCommand returns nil at security.go:26-29 and executor.go:163 runs any executable.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only the no-config default is what the advisory talks about; a user who points at their own file is presumed to know its semantics, and the built-in defaults are documented as applying when no file is given.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: config.go, one file and the same package away; the check (security.go:26) never calls the loader that produced the flag

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `use_shell_execution: true` legacy mode: the raw string goes to bash -c after only substring allow/blocklist checks, with no metacharacter scan and no executable allowlist.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: README:60 and security-legacy.yaml:1-9 label this mode VULNERABLE and handler_test.go:134-152 asserts it stays vulnerable, so it is explicitly not secure mode.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: security.go -> executor.go:146, same package, two files

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second MCP tool (e.g. `shell_run` taking `commands []string` or `script`) that calls executor.execute without validator.validateCommand
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already wraps a single tool over the executor; MCP clients asking for batch or pipeline execution make a second tool the obvious next feature, and only the handler wires in the validator.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An alternative policy source (inline MCP_SHELL_SEC_CONFIG_JSON env or a --security flag) that builds SecurityConfig without the file loader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: loadConfig and main.go:35 already branch on env vars; a maintainer adding a flag would repeat the anonymous-struct mapping and drop the enabled/merge semantics.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A defaults-merge helper that keeps the built-in allowlist and appends the file's allowed_executables when the file list is empty or partial
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix introduces newDefaultSecurityConfig, so 'merge file over defaults' is the natural follow-up, and interpreter names from the file slip in beside the safe list.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shell-syntax fallback that runs `sh -c` when the command contains a pipe or glob the direct-exec path cannot express
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The bash -c branch already exists for legacy mode, so reusing it for 'complex' commands that clients request is a one-line change away.

O9_family: insecure default configuration plus permissive allowlist leading to OS command execution (CWE-1188 / CWE-183 / CWE-78)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25 (go.mod:3); Makefile:21-27 `go build`, module deps resolved from go.sum (no vendor dir), so the first build needs the module cache or network
O10_build.project_tests: `go test ./...` (Makefile:70-71): security_test.go (validateCommand / allowlist / metachars / blocked patterns), executor_test.go (parseCommand, secure vs legacy execution), handler_test.go (end-to-end handler including injection-prevention cases), config_test.go (defaults and YAML loading)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip /bin/bash, /usr/bin/python3 and /usr/bin/git from security.yaml (and add '!' to the metacharacter set), leaving Enabled:false as the built-in default and the config loader's zero-value override in place.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit f31377f also closes a different advisory, GHSA-74hp-mggr-hv58 (git `-c alias.x=!cmd`); the '!' and "=!" hunks in security.go:163-180 belong to that one, not to this advisory's interpreter-default issue.
